verdicts.note: On discrete-fourier-transform, m is an exponent of omega with 0<m<q; the input count m of a linear map is a different thing. The later DFT page should use another letter for the exponent, or say explicitly that m here is an exponent, not the input count.

On tensor-product, u is an s-by-t array with entries u_hg; the linear map's u is a vector of m complex numbers. The later tensor-product page should use another letter for the array, or say that u here is an array, not an input vector.

On tensor-product, m is an output column index; the linear map's m is the input count. The later tensor-product page should use another letter for the column index, or say it is a column index, not the input count.

On radix-digit-convolution, a is the list of radix digits of x (length d, integer digits a_0..a_{d-1}); on the DFT page a is a generic vector of q complex numbers. The later page should use another letter for the digit list (for example a digit name tied to x), or say that a here is the digit list, padded to length q only when transformed.

On radix-digit-convolution, e is a digit position running over 0..d-1; on the DFT page e is an integer exponent of omega. The later radix page should use another letter for the digit position, or say that e here is a digit position, not an exponent.

On radix-digit-convolution, z is a formal polynomial variable; on exact-integer-multiplication z is a nonnegative integer below 2^k. The later radix page should use another letter for the formal variable, or say that z here is a formal variable, not an integer.

On radix-digit-convolution, b is the digit list of y (length d); on the DFT page b is a generic second vector of q complex numbers. The later radix page should use another letter for the digit list, or say that b here is the digit list of y.

On radix-digit-convolution, c is the coefficient list of the product a(z)b(z), i.e. the convolution; on the DFT page c is the entrywise product of transforms. The later radix page should use another letter for the convolution, or say that c here is the convolution of the digit lists.

On gaussian-resampling, s is the source length; on the DFT page s is a frequency summation index running over 0..q-1. The later gaussian-resampling page should use another letter for the frequency index, or say that s here is the source length and not a summation index.

On gaussian-resampling, p is the integer precision of the approximation; on radix-digit-convolution p is a coefficient index of c. The later gaussian-resampling page should use another letter for the precision, or say that p here is the precision, not a coefficient index.

On gaussian-resampling, p is the integer precision; on the DFT page p is an output position running over 0..q-1. The later gaussian-resampling page should use another letter for the precision, or say that p here is the precision, not an output position.

On transform-identity, F_s is first the one-dimensional transform F_q with q=s; on convolution-theorem F_s is the transform applied along every axis, normalized by 1/S. Once lifted, transform-identity uses F_s in the multi-axis sense, so the page should use another letter for the one-dimensional transform, or say explicitly where F_s means the lifted transform.

On transform-identity, d is the number of coordinates of the grid; on radix-digit-convolution d is the number of radix digits of each input. The later transform-identity page should use another letter for the coordinate count, or say that d here is the coordinate count, not the digit count (as it already does in part).

On transform-identity, u is an array on a grid of shape s_1 x ... x s_d; on linear-map u is a vector of m complex numbers. The later page should use another letter for the array, or say that u here is an array on the source grid, not an input vector.

On transform-identity, v is a second array on the source grid; on linear-map v is the output vector of k complex numbers. The later page should use another letter for the array, or say that v here is a source-grid array, not an output vector.
